entities.name: Siege of Dubrovnik
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Siege of Dubrovnik was a pivotal 1991-1992 military operation in which the Yugoslav People's Army and Serb paramilitaries besieged the historic city of Dubrovnik, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, in what is now modern-day Croatia. The 1991 October 1st to 1992 May 31st siege lasted for 7 months and resulted in significant damage to the city's medieval architecture.

 The city's defenders, mostly made up of Croatian soldiers and local civilians, fought bravely against the vastly superior Serb forces, using the city's medieval walls and fortifications to their advantage. The siege was ultimately lifted on May 31st, 1992, but not before the city suffered significant damage and loss of life.

 The Siege of Dubrovnik had a lasting impact on the region, contributing to the escalation of the Yugoslav Wars and the eventual independence of Croatia. The city's rich cultural heritage was severely damaged, and the siege remains a painful reminder of the devastating consequences of war.

 As Dubrovnik's mayor, Mato Andrić-Lužović, said in 1992, 'The siege of Dubrovnik was a dramatic moment in the history of our city, a moment that will be remembered for generations to come.'
